profile.address: 800, Willamette Street, College Hill, Eugene, Lane County, Oregon, 97401
profile.reading:
Date Center West - Eugene, the "Date" in the name is very likely a data-entry typo for "Data" carried over from OpenStreetMap, is one of two facilities operated by Data Center West, Inc., an independent, privately held colocation and managed-services provider founded in 2004 and based in Southern Oregon. The company's core market is Medford, Ashland, Klamath Falls, and Grants Pass, and it markets itself as the largest independent colocation and cloud-services provider in Southern Oregon and Northern California. The Eugene site, roughly 165 miles north in the Willamette Valley, is its smaller secondary location, extending that regional footprint north along Interstate 5.

Data Center West publishes real, if modest, technical specifications for its facilities rather than treating them as unpublished. The Eugene site has 500 square feet of raised technical floor space rated to carry more than 800 pounds per square foot, a floor load specification aimed at server racks and storage arrays rather than a general office build-out, with dedicated 110, 208, and 220-volt electrical circuits. Power resilience comes from telco-standard DC power service backed by the building's own diesel generator, and cooling is handled by 5-ton air-conditioning units. Fire detection uses smoke, heat, and thermal alarms rather than a gas-based suppression system, and the site has two separate fiber entry points, a basic but meaningful form of physical carrier diversity for a facility this size. By comparison, the company's larger Medford facility runs to 2,000 square feet with a dedicated Caterpillar 3412 diesel generator and four 5-ton AC units, underscoring that Eugene is deliberately the smaller of the company's two data halls.

What Data Center West does not publish for Eugene is a specific street address on its own site, a megawatt or kilowatt IT-capacity figure, or a formal Tier or uptime certification. That is consistent with the scale of the business. This is a small, regional, privately held colocation operator serving local businesses in a secondary market, not a wholesale or hyperscale operator competing nationally on published capacity numbers. The facility exists to give Eugene-area businesses, likely including local government, healthcare, education, and small-business tenants, reliable rack space and internet connectivity without having to reach north to Portland or contract with a national colocation brand for a modest hosting need.

reading.body:
Data Center West operates a facility in Eugene, Oregon, but its capacity is not published. The operator describes itself as an independent colocation and cloud services provider serving Southern Oregon and Northern California since 2004, though Eugene's inclusion under this operator has not been individually confirmed and may require verification.

Oregon has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which only 8 publish capacity figures totaling 156.6 MW. This Eugene facility does not appear in that published total. Without a stated capacity, it cannot be ranked against other Oregon sites or assessed against the state's known infrastructure footprint.

The absence of published specifications limits any reading of this facility's relevance to AI scaling. To determine whether it matters to the grid constraint on compute, a reader would need confirmed capacity figures from the operator, current power delivery to the site, and details on whether infrastructure supports the density required for modern accelerator workloads.
